sections.title: Model overview and intended purpose
sections.text: legacy-r-logistic, recorded as 'Credit default logistic regression (legacy)', estimates the probability that a credit-card customer defaults in the next month and is described as being used in credit decisions; it is assigned risk tier 1. The model name, business purpose and train fraction are inferred fields, and the formal business purpose, intended use, portfolio scope, model owner and developer are not documented. The code is a development fixture standing in for the real model, not the production model, and it uses the public UCI 'Default of Credit Card Clients' dataset (30,000 records, 23 input variables, Taiwan credit-card clients, April to September 2005), which is described as demonstration data only and not representative of a UK bank's current portfolio.

sections.title: Algorithm and methodology
sections.text: The model is a logistic regression implemented in R using glm with a binomial family and logit link, predicting default.payment.next.month from 21 input features: LIMIT_BAL, EDUCATION, MARRIAGE, the repayment status variables PAY_0 and PAY_2 to PAY_6, bill amounts BILL_AMT1 to BILL_AMT6, and payment amounts PAY_AMT1 to PAY_AMT6. ID, SEX and AGE are excluded from modelling, with SEX and AGE recorded as retained only for fairness review. Data is read from data/processed/credit_default_clean.csv and split into train and test sets with a stratified split on the target (test_size=0.2, random_state=42), giving an 80/20 split, and the R model applies no further transformation. A decision threshold of 0.35 is applied, but the rationale for this threshold is not documented.

sections.title: Limitations and assumptions
sections.text: No validation metrics, calibration or threshold justification are computed, and no performance results, fairness review results for SEX and AGE, monitoring plan, or approval and version history are documented. EDUCATION, MARRIAGE and the PAY_x variables are assumed to enter the model as read by read_csv, likely as numeric rather than categorical, which may not reflect their nature. The data source, observation period, target definition details and the cleaning steps that produce credit_default_clean.csv are not documented. Because the code is a development fixture trained on public demonstration data, its outputs should not be taken as representative of the production model or of a UK bank's current portfolio.
